title: Dedicated Safeguard Allocator and Soft Preemption PRD
creator: Sofia Alvarez
body:
Overview:
This PRD defines the 'Safeguard Allocator' — a runtime + control-plane feature that prevents catastrophic tenant interference in Redwood Dedicated capacity pools by combining a configurable soft-preemption mechanism with fractional headroom allocation and tenant credit smoothing. The goal is to protect reserved customers' latency and throughput SLOs while allowing short, bounded bursts for other tenants without permanent capacity starvation.

Problem Statement:
- Tenants with reserved capacity occasionally experience severe SLA regressions when bursty cross-traffic or noisy workloads expand KV cache pressure and tail latency spikes.
- Current hard preemption (eviction) is disruptive, often causing request failures or long cold starts for victims.
- Operators lack a single knob that enforces tenant guarantees while enabling safe, short-duration bursts for lower-priority workloads.

Objectives (success criteria):
- Guarantee P99 latency and throughput headroom for reserved tenants within configured SLAs during steady-state and transient bursts.
- Reduce the number of hard preemptions by >= 80% in the first three months after rollout for participating pools.
- Provide observability and audit trails for all soft-preemption decisions and reclaimed capacity, surfaced in Console and logs.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not redesign the entire autoscaling algorithm. It augments existing scaling with a capacity-safeguard layer.
- It does not change billing models; billing impacts (if any) will be handled by a separate PM workstream.

Design Overview:
1) Fractional headroom allocator:
   - Each reserved tenant has a configurable minimum reserved allocation (baseline) and a small fractional headroom buffer (e.g., 5-20% of baseline) held in soft state to absorb burst variance without touching other tenants.
   - Headroom is represented as a lease token in the control plane with expiration and renewal semantics.

2) Tenant credit smoothing ledger:
   - Tenants accumulate transient-use credits when they underutilize baseline over a configurable time window. Credits allow temporary borrowing beyond baseline during bursts. Credits decay over time to prevent long-term debt.

3) Soft preemption policy engine:
   - When pressure exceeds pool capacity, the engine attempts gentle throttles: rate limits, batch size reductions, and prioritized request queuing tied to tenant priority and credit balance.
   - If gentle measures don't suffice, the system soft-preempts by revoking non-critical headroom leases and enforcing graceful degradation (queue backoffs, reduced concurrency) before any hard eviction.

4) Emergency reclaim and auditing:
   - If reclaim is required to protect a P0 reserved tenant, an emergency reclaim is issued with stepwise mitigations and a timeline for automatic rollback or operator decision. All actions are logged and visible in Console with a replayable event timeline.

API/Console Surface:
- New API fields on Dedicated tenant configs: "baseline_capacity", "headroom_pct", "credit_window_minutes", "preemption_tier".
- Console UI: Capacity -> Safeguards tab showing active headroom leases, credit balances, recent soft-preempts, and a simulation tool to preview guardrail behavior for hypothetical bursts.

Requirements (must-have):
requirements: R1: Control-plane must maintain per-tenant baseline and headroom tokens with TTL and renewal logic.
R2: Runtime must expose low-overhead hooks to check and enforce headroom tokens without adding >3% tail-latency overhead under load.
R3: Soft preemption engine must support a configurable policy chain: gentle throttles -> deprioritization -> headroom revoke -> emergency reclaim.
R4: Console must display a searchable audit log of all safeguard actions with tenant, pool, timestamp, reason, and outcome.
R5: Provide SDK/REST API to set and get safeguard configs; errors must be validated and surfaced with actionable messages.
R6: Telemetry: emit metrics for headroom usage, credit balances, soft-preempt counts, and hard eviction fallback events (if any).
R7: Backwards compatibility: tenants without safeguard configs must default to existing behavior (no sudden changes).
R8: Security: safeguard control-plane operations must be auditable and gated by RBAC (only operators and tenant admins can change critical settings).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Can create/update tenant safeguard config via API and Console; new config persisted and enforced within 60s.

AC2: Under controlled burst test (see test harness), reserved tenant P99 latency remains within configured SLA for 95% of runs while non-reserved tenants observe graceful degradation rather than hard failures.
AC3: Soft-preempt actions are visible in Console with a link to the audit event and a machine-readable log entry in the platform logs.
AC4: Headroom tokens automatically expire after TTL and auto-renew only if renewal criteria (low pressure, credits) are met.
AC5: Metrics emitted to metrics pipeline: guard.safeguard.headroom_usage, guard.safeguard.credit_balance, guard.safeguard.soft_preempt_count with correct tenant tags.
AC6: Canary rollout (5% of Dedicated pools) shows >=80% reduction in hard evictions compared to matched control pools over 7 days.
AC7: No privilege escalation or RBAC bypass observed in security audit of control-plane APIs.
success_metrics: Metric 1: Hard evictions per 10k requests for reserved tenants decreases by >=80% after rollout.
Metric 2: Average P99 latency for reserved tenants within SLA in 95% of measured windows during bursts.
Metric 3: Number of emergency reclaims per week per pool <= 0.1 for steady-state pools.
Metric 4: Operator MTTR for capacity incidents reduced by 25% due to clearer auditing and tooling.
Metric 5: Adoption: >=30% of active dedicated tenants opt in to safeguards within 90 days of general availability.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design + infra spike (2 sprints) - implement control-plane token store and basic telemetry. Phase 1: Pilot inside one regional Dedicated pool with internal tenants (canary 5%) for 2 weeks; run synthetic burst suite and measure. Phase 2: Broader beta with selected customers and product-led opt-in (4 weeks); gather feedback and iterate. Phase 3: GA for all Dedicated pools with doc, SDK, and support playbooks. Operator training and runbook updates required before GA.
dependencies: DEP-ENG-CORE: Runtime hook for headroom token checks (engineer: Priya Nair)
DEP-PLATFORM: Control-plane token store and TTL semantics (engineer: Omar El-Sayed)
DEP-CONSOLE: Safeguards UI, audit log viewer (designer: Lina Gomez)
DEP-METRICS: New metrics and dashboards (owner: DataInfra team)
DEP-SEC: RBAC policy review and auditability (security: Arun Desai)
DEP-QA: Synthetic burst test harness and chaos scenarios (QA: Nolan Reed)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Headroom tokens add control-plane churn and increased latency. Mitigation: keep tokens lightweight, TTL batching, and local cache on runtime nodes.
Risk: Soft preemption policies might be gamed by tenants to hog credits. Mitigation: credit decay, burst rate limits, and operator alerts for abnormal credit accrual.
Risk: Unexpected edge-case causes hard evictions to spike. Mitigation: staged canary, automated rollback, and throttled GA with operator approval.
Risk: Customers confused by new knobs. Mitigation: clear Console simulations, recommended presets, and in-product guidance.
open_questions: Q1: Default headroom_pct recommended for small vs large tenants? (suggested: 10% small, 5% large)
Q2: Should credits be transferrable across pools in same organization? Security and accounting implications to consider.
Q3: How to reflect soft-preempt events in billing (if at all)? Decide in parallel billing PM thread.
Q4: TTL/renewal backoff strategy under network partitions - prefer conservative expiry or optimistic extension?
notes: Implementation spike: evaluate two approaches for headroom token store: Kubernetes CRD backed vs dedicated fast KV (Redis/etcd).
Benchmarks: early microbench shows <2% added CPU on runtime path for headroom checks when implemented in native C++ layer.
Related docs: link to internal design brainstorming doc (confluence://dedicated/safeguard-allocator), simulation harness PR (#4567 in GH).
